column5:
'- the digital student card does not have the EU certified student card logo and is fully in Dutch, making it difficult to use it to get a student discount outside of the Netherlands (for example to access a museum while on vacation). Often, it kind of ends up like "I'm a student, just trust me. My university doesn't offer physical student cards for some reason" and then it's up to the poor employee having to judge whether or not I'm lying. It is awkward, frustrating, and entirely avoidable by simply having an internationally recognised card like everyone else.

- loading the app, logging in, and using the 2FA takes a lot of time, which often results in me causing a delay and making people wait. This creates frustration in me, the person serving me and people behind me in line. If I'm on my phone in line to open it in advance that's rude, if I don't have it open yet that's also rude. You cannot win. And ofc there is the often recurring frustrating situation where an employee asks for my student card, I go to open the app, this takes forever, a line forms behind me, and RIGHT as I'm almost there, the employee goes "Never mind, I believe you're a student". In short, the long time it takes to start up makes it frustrating and unpleasant to use, causing trouble to not just myself but also others.

- It is above here as well, but I cannot stress enough how annoying it is to need to have a charged phone with access to wifi or 4G on you at all times. It makes navigating the world if your phone dies or breaks, or if you're in a place without 4G or wifi nearly impossible. Not to mention that not everyone can afford unlimited data. And especially when studying! It is well-known that having your phone on your person when studying makes it harder to concentrate. The n1 study tip every professional gives is to put your phone in a different room. What does the university do? Make this physically impossible! It makes no sense to me.
column8:
Please start offering a variety of options. It's fine if the online card is the only free one, but let students pick which option serves them and their needs best.

And while we're at it, please also consider giving more options for 2FA than just the one that requires a smartphone. I understand that via text is more likely to be intercepted, but if it's safe enough for access to government agencies like DUO and the belastingdienst, it's also safe enough for access to a student's grades or homework. If the text option is only available for the app and Brightspace, which students use daily, but not for Osiris, which carries the most sensitive information, I think that would already be a win.

column8: The university makes the argument that it is somehow easy to fake a student ID card. However, it is way, WAY easier to fake a letter of enrollment. On top of that, they make an argument that the cards are hard to retract. I disagree! If you need to scan your card when you come in and the computer checks against a central database, then erasing an entry is trivial. Boom! Card de-activated. The current system is also easy to fake, since you can take a screenshot and put that on your phone. You can even edit the screenshot. I can say from experience that this method works, which is not possible with a physical card that you scan. What a dumb reasoning!
